papers.title_in_file: Enhancing Quantum Machine Learning with Anyons
papers.version_note: arXiv:2606.16090v1, 15 Jun 2026. The main text and Appendices A and B are in the text layer; the Supplementary Information (sections III and IV) is cited but not part of this text.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a photonic quantum kernel family that interpolates between bosonic, anyon-inspired fractional and fermionic exchange phases, assessed by effective dimension, kernel geometry and MNIST and Fashion-MNIST classification.

existing.note: The effective-dimension result is a numerical Haar-average for N = 2, 3 and 4 particles in M = 6 modes. The derivation (projector decomposition, sector entropies, partial-Pauli bounds) is only referred to in the Supplementary Information, so no statement of a theorem or proof appears in the text.
existing.value: The authors state that a Haar-averaged effective-dimension analysis, evaluated for N = 2, 3, and 4 particles distributed across M = 6 modes, shows a pronounced increase of the effective dimension in the fractional statistical region, and that fractional exchange phases access feature-space directions inaccessible to the purely symmetric or antisymmetric limits; the supporting projector decomposition, sector-resolved entropy contributions and partial-Pauli bounds are given in the Supplementary Information.

The effective dimension for N = 2, 3, and 4 particles distributed across M = 6 modes is illustrated in Fig. 2a.
In the fractional statistical region, a pronounced increase in Deff(ϕ) is observed.
The corresponding central projector decomposition, sector-resolved entropy contributions, and partial-Pauli bounds are given in the Supplementary Information section III.
existing.certainty_reason: A numerical result for three particle numbers in six modes; the analytic support is in the Supplementary Information, not quoted here.
existing.reader_inference: The main text gives no proof that the enhancement holds for other N or M; it is shown for three cases.

existing.note: The text supports the highest accuracies at intermediate phases on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST for N = 2, 3 and 4, simulated. Kernel-target alignment and inter-class distance are shown for the two-particle kernel only. The comparison is with the bosonic and fermionic limits and a distinguishable-photon baseline; the text states no comparison with a classical kernel, and gives no accuracy values in the text (they are in Fig. 3).
existing.value: The authors report that on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, for N = 2, 3 and 4 particles, the highest test accuracies of the kernel SVM are obtained at intermediate fractional exchange phases, and that kernels incorporating anyonic exchange consistently outperform both bosonic and fermionic limits; kernel-target alignment and mean inter-class distance, shown for the two-particle kernel, both favour an intermediate exchange phase biased towards the fermionic side.
existing.anchor: Section I p.3; Section V pp.10-12; Fig. 3
quotes: Across these tasks, kernels incorporating anyonic exchange consistently outperform both bosonic and fermionic limits.
As shown in Fig. 3a,b, the classification accuracies on both the MNIST and the Fashion-MNIST datasets are plotted for N = 2, 3 and 4 particles, with exchange phase ϕ ∈ [0, π].
For both datasets, it turns out that the highest accuracies are obtained at intermediate fractional exchange phases.
both quantities favour an intermediate exchange phase biased towards the fermionic side, matching the regime in which the highest test accuracy is observed.
existing.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulated study.
existing.reader_inference: All results are simulations on two image datasets after PCA; no classical-kernel accuracy is given in the text.

we utilized the input state |0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0⟩ for two particles, |0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0⟩ for three particles, and |0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0⟩ for four particles.

assertions.value: The authors state that the geometric difference and model-complexity ratio were computed on binary tasks restricted to classes 0 and 3 of MNIST and Fashion-MNIST with 100 class-balanced samples per instance, and that the full classification was evaluated on all 10 classes, trained on 6,000 class-balanced samples and tested on 1,000 class-balanced test samples, with ten independent random dataset splits for every task.
quotes: we constructed binary classification tasks restricted to classes 0 and 3 from both the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets [37, 38]. Each of these random instances comprised 100 class-balanced samples.

the evaluation was expanded to include all 10 classes from both datasets. In these multiclass scenarios, the models were trained on 6,000 class-balanced samples and subsequently evaluated on 1,000 class-balanced test samples.
To ensure robust statistical reliability, ten independent random dataset splits were generated for every task.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own evaluation setup in Appendix A.
assertions.reader_inference: The geometry results rest on 100-sample binary tasks, a small sample for a kernel inverse in Eq. (15).

assertions.value: The authors state that classical data were compressed by PCA, each retained feature component was normalized to the interval [0, 1], and the components were assigned to the parameters of a programmable Clements-type interferometer of Mach-Zehnder interferometers, with two assigned feature components fixing the beamsplitter angle and internal phase of each interferometer.

After PCA, each retained feature component was normalized to the interval [0, 1] before being assigned to the optical parameters.
two assigned feature components determine the beamsplitter angle and internal phase according to θℓ = πx2ℓ−1 and φℓ = 2πx2ℓ, respectively.

assertions.value: The authors state that the optical simulation reproduces the exchange-phase-dependent interference expected for Abelian anyonic exchange at the level of measured correlation probabilities for two photons, and that for N > 2 the construction should be interpreted more narrowly as an anyon-inspired feature map defined on particle permutations.
quotes: For two photons, the optical simulation reproduces the exchange-phase-dependent interference expected for Abelian anyonic exchange at the level of measured correlation probabilities.
For N > 2, the construction should be interpreted more narrowly as an anyon-inspired feature map defined on particle permutations.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own model in Appendix B.
assertions.reader_inference: The three- and four-particle results are for the permutation-level model, not for physical anyons.

assertions.value: The authors state that, unlike physical anyons, which are described by braid-group representations, their model does not resolve braid histories, exchange orientations or winding processes, and retains only the induced element of the permutation group SN, assigning the exchange phase through the inversion number.
quotes: Unlike physical anyons, which are described by braid-group representations, our model does not resolve braid histories, exchange orientations, or winding processes
Instead, it retains only the induced element of the permutation group SN and assigns an exchange phase through the inversion number π(σ).

assertions.value: The authors report that increasing the particle number improves the performance of both the bosonic and fractional-statistics kernels, while the performance of the fermionic kernel does not improve with particle number and its lowest accuracy is found for N = 4 fermions.
quotes: Fig. 3a,b also show that increasing the particle number improves the performance of both the bosonic and fractional-statistics kernels.
Its performance does not improve with particle number, and the lowest accuracy is found for N = 4 fermions.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulated study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the optimal phase for accuracy is shifted towards the fermionic side of the fractional-statistics regime, rather than coinciding with the maxima of the geometry-only diagnostics.
quotes: we observe that the optimal phase is shifted towards the fermionic side of the fractional-statistics regime, rather than coinciding with the maxima of the geometry-only diagnostics discussed above.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulated study.
assertions.reader_inference: The geometry diagnostics therefore do not select the best phase for accuracy; the authors' closing claim that they guide design is weaker than it reads.

assertions.value: The authors suggest that the fermionic endpoint suppresses class separation through Pauli exclusion, while the bosonic endpoint enhances separation through bunching but yields weaker agreement with the target labels, and that fractional statistics balance these limits so that the classification advantage arises from a kernel geometry that is both well separated and well aligned with the task.
quotes: Physically, the fermionic endpoint suppresses class separation through Pauli exclusion, whereas the bosonic endpoint enhances separation through bunching but yields weaker agreement with the target labels.

The concurrent enhancement of KTA and dinter therefore suggests that the classification advantage arises from a fractional-statistics kernel geometry that is both well separated and well aligned with the learning task.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author interpretation, not tested by an ablation in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: A correlation of alignment and distance with accuracy; the paper does not test that it is the cause.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that exchange statistics are a structural ingredient for quantum machine learning, that the fractional-statistics kernel can reduce the model complexity required to represent the observed labels, and that geometric diagnostics evaluated before supervised training can provide useful guidance for designing quantum kernels with improved predictive performance.
quotes: In this work, we identify exchange statistics as a structural ingredient for quantum machine learning.
Together, these results show that geometric diagnostics, evaluated before supervised training, can provide useful guidance for designing quantum kernels with improved predictive performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' conclusion from one simulated study.
assertions.reader_inference: Section V reports that the best-accuracy phase differs from the geometry maxima, so the guidance claim holds for the regime, not the optimum.

assertions.value: The authors claim that their work identifies particle exchange statistics as an overlooked computational ingredient for quantum machine learning and provides the first systematic comparison of quantum learning models across exchange phases.
quotes: Our work identifies particle exchange statistics as an overlooked computational ingredient for quantum machine learning and provides the first systematic comparison of quantum learning models across exchange phases.
assertions.certainty_reason: A priority claim made by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that they used a universal Clements interferometer as a generic photonic encoder, and that universality alone does not guarantee that the resulting feature map is well matched to a given learning problem.
quotes: Here we used a universal Clements interferometer as a generic photonic encoder.
universality alone does not guarantee that the resulting feature map is well matched to a given learning problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit in Section VI.

assertions.value: The authors state that extending to larger particle numbers does not require physical anyons or real-space braiding, and that entangled photon inputs with a tunable relative phase have already been used to emulate a continuous interpolation between bosonic and fermionic behavior under linear optical evolution, citing earlier work.
quotes: Entangled photon inputs with a tunable relative phase have already been used to emulate a continuous interpolation between bosonic and fermionic behavior under linear optical evolution [29]
but it does not require physical anyons or real-space braiding.
assertions.certainty_reason: The emulation is attributed to prior work.
